edits.old:
A guest with a serious allergy needs their meal to reach them, not the person in the next chair. Open seating makes that harder.

In Australia, food businesses must be able to tell you about allergens: for food that doesn't carry a label, such as food served at a café, [allergen declarations must be displayed in connection with the food or provided to the purchaser on request](https://www.foodstandards.gov.au/business/labelling/allergen-labelling). <!-- fact_100 --> Under the Food Standards Code, the allergens that must be declared include peanut, sesame, egg, milk, fish, crustacean, mollusc, soy, wheat, lupin, almond, Brazil nut, cashew, hazelnut, macadamia, pecan, pistachio, pine nut and walnut, while [barley, oats and rye must be declared if they contain gluten](https://www.foodstandards.gov.au/business/labelling/allergen-labelling). <!-- fact_101 --> The stakes are real: a food allergy reaction [can include anaphylaxis](https://www.foodstandards.gov.au/business/labelling/allergen-labelling). <!-- fact_102 -->

That obligation sits with your caterer, not with you, and this is general information rather than legal advice. The practical lesson is simple: give your caterer the list of guest allergies early, whatever your seating. For a wedding overseas, don't assume Australian rules apply: ask the venue how its kitchen handles allergens and how it will make sure each meal reaches the right guest.
edits.new:

In Australia, for food that doesn't carry a label, [allergen declarations must be displayed in connection with the food or provided to the purchaser on request](https://www.foodstandards.gov.au/business/labelling/allergen-labelling). <!-- fact_100 --> That obligation sits with your caterer, and this is general information rather than legal advice. For a wedding overseas, don't assume Australian rules apply: ask the venue how its kitchen handles allergens and how each meal will reach the right guest.

edits.old: In Australia, when food isn't in packaging or doesn't need a label, [allergen information must be displayed with the food or can be requested from the supplier](https://www.foodstandards.gov.au/consumer/labelling/allergen-labelling). <!-- fact_103 --> At a wedding, that supplier is your caterer: give them the list early, ask how special meals will be identified and served, and agree whether guests with allergies sit at a known table so their plates reach them.
edits.new: Then ask your caterer how special meals will be identified and served, and agree whether guests with allergies sit at a known table so their plates reach them.
